A content delivery network, or CDN, is a system of computers spread across many cities and countries that work together to deliver websites, videos, and images faster. Without one, every request for a webpage would travel all the way back to a single origin server — the main computer where the original files live, often located in just one place. That trip can be slow, especially for people far from that location.

To speed things up, a CDN stores copies of the same files on many computers positioned closer to where people actually are. Each of these nearby computers is called an edge location, since it sits at the edge of the network, near the audience rather than at the center. Think of it like a chain of neighborhood libraries that each keep popular books on hand, so readers do not need to travel to one giant central library every time.

When someone requests a file, the system first checks the nearest edge location. If that copy is already there and ready to use, it is called a cache hit, and the file is delivered almost instantly. If not, the edge location fetches a fresh copy from the origin server, saves it for next time, and passes it along.

The result is a web that feels quicker and more reliable, because most requests get answered by a nearby location instead of a distant one, reducing delays, easing congestion, and helping websites stay available even during heavy traffic or partial outages.

| Term | Plain meaning | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| CDN | A network of computers in many locations that store copies of the same content | Spreads out the work so no single place gets overwhelmed |
| Origin server | The main computer holding the original, master copy of a file | Everything ultimately traces back here if no copy exists elsewhere |
| Edge location | A computer positioned close to a group of people, holding stored copies | Shortens the distance content has to travel, making delivery faster |
| Cache hit | A successful find of a requested file already stored at a nearby location | Means near-instant delivery without contacting the origin server |
